subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call SLOs & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - follow up + SLO confirmation

Hi Elena —

Great to meet today. Thanks for walking through FinTech Inc's production workload and priorities. Quick recap and a few asks so we can scope Dedicated capacity sizing and a short performance validation run: 

Recap / priorities:
- Primary objective: ensure dedicated pool can meet latency SLOs for customer-facing flows while keeping unit cost predictable.
- Workload mix: 70% short completions (chat-style, 50-150 tokens), 30% long-form generation (summaries, 400-800 tokens).
- Models: mixture of open medium/large models (you mentioned gpt-medium-30b for long-form and a smaller 8b variant for chat).

Questions / SLOs we need confirmed from your side:
1) Latency SLOs (p95): what are target numbers for short completions and long-form? (e.g., p95 <= 250ms short, <= 1200ms long)
2) Concurrency and throughput: sustained RPS and expected concurrency per model type (sustained qps, peak burst).
3) Streaming: do you require partial-token streaming for the chat path? Any maximum chunk interval requirement?
4) Typical sequence lengths: average & max prompt tokens + expected generated tokens (helpful for KV cache sizing).

Next steps we propose:
- You can fill the attached sizing template (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) with a 48h sample of traffic (timestamps, model, prompt tokens, response tokens).
- We’ll run a 4-hour dedicated capacity validation in our sandbox: 1) baseline throughput test, 2) streaming latency verification, 3) burst/scale behaviour.
- Optional: we can run GPU comparisons (H100 vs A100) for your critical paths if you want to validate cost/latency trade-offs.

Could you confirm the SLOs and send a 48h sample or the anonymized peak profile? I’ve cc'd Aditya to coordinate the validation window and internal SRE resources.

Best,
Marissa

From: Elena Rossi <elena@fintechinc.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - follow up + SLO confirmation

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming our targets and adding some detail from our side:

SLOs / workload details
- Short completions (customer chat): p95 latency target = 200ms (we can tolerate up to 250ms in 5% of cases). Streaming required with token-chunk deliver every 150ms max.
- Long-form generation (summaries / batch jobs): p95 target = 900ms for 400-600 tokens; we can accept up to 1.5s for 800-token outputs.

Throughput / concurrency
- Sustained: ~20 RPS across the account, with 60% routed to the small model and 40% to the medium model.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent requests = 40, peak concurrency observed = 120 during market open spikes.
- Burst behavior: short bursts up to ~300 RPS for 10-15s during heavy events.

Models and payloads
- Models: "gpt-small-8b" (chat) and "gpt-medium-30b" (summaries).
- Avg prompt tokens: 60 (chat), 150 (summaries). Avg response tokens: 120 (chat), 500 (summaries).

We attached an anonymized peak profile (fintech_peak_profile.csv) showing 48h traffic; hope this helps with sizing. For compliance we will need a short MSA addendum around data handling on Dedicated; procurement will follow up.

Next steps: please send a sizing proposal and an outline for the 4-hour validation run. We’re good to run the validation next week (any day after Tue 14 Jul).

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product Operations, FinTech Inc
elena@fintechinc.com

Attachments: fintech_peak_profile.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@fintechinc.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - follow up + SLO confirmation

Elena —

Appreciate the detail and the profile — that’s exactly what we need. High-level sizing notes and proposal: 

1) Quick sizing callouts (based on your 48h sample):
- Sustained 20 RPS with peak bursts to 300 RPS and peak concurrency 120 points to needing reserved capacity with autoscale headroom.
- For the chat path (p95 200ms streaming): H100-based pool looks promising for best latency; A100 80GB can meet p95 for many short requests but gives less headroom on bursts without increased cluster size.
- For summaries (p95 900ms for ~500 tokens): a medium pool of A100s with optimized batching/kv cache and quantized model variant should comfortably meet targets at lower cost.

2) GPU comparison (what we’ll validate in sandbox):
- H100 80GB: lower p95 for short streaming paths, better for sustained high concurrency; higher hourly cost.
- A100 80GB: good cost/throughput balance for long-form; may need more nodes to cover bursty 300 RPS peaks.

3) Proposed reserved throughput / initial configuration for validation:
- Dedicated pool 1 (chat): 8x H100 nodes, reserved throughput target ~200k tokens/min (allows ~250 RPS baseline for short completions with streaming enabled).
- Dedicated pool 2 (summaries): 6x A100 nodes, reserved throughput target tuned for sustained 20 RPS with batching.

4) Validation plan (4 hours):
- Phase A (baseline): run sustained workload from your sample for 60 minutes to verify p95 and token accounting.
- Phase B (burst): replay peak bursts (300 RPS) to validate autoscale/fallback and tail latency.
- Phase C (streaming): focused streaming latency checks with 150ms chunking requirement.
- Phase D (cost run): record token costs and GPU utilization to refine committed capacity recommendation.

I’ve attached a short sizing proposal PDF (redwood-sizing-proposal.pdf) with the above plus preliminary cost ballpark. If that looks good, we’ll: 
- Confirm the validation window for Wed 15 Jul or Thu 16 Jul (you said any day after Tue 14 Jul).
- We’ll provision sandbox pools and give you an access URL and a test API key with masked data routing.

Would you like both H100 and A100 comparison runs during the same validation window or run H100 for chat and A100 for summaries as a first pass?

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-sizing-proposal.pdf
